Subject: BrightLane evaluation exchange - sandbox + MAP proposal

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightLane is ready to move to a short pilot (2-week) using our retail QA suite. We can provide: the prompt pack (zipped), a manifest of ~1.2k test cases, and a small seed dataset.

Request / asks from our side:
- A mutual action plan (MPA) that targets a pilot kickoff next Tuesday (2028-01-17) and an acceptance window ending 2028-01-31.
- Limited-use, ephemeral sandbox: BrightLane needs assurance data will be isolated and deleted after the acceptance window.
- Audit trail / transfer: S3 signed-transfer and retention logs for audit.
- License: Narrow, evaluation-only usage; no production inference, no indexing.

We can upload the artifacts to an S3 staging bucket once we have the MPA signed and a transfer contact. Attaching a high-level inventory now.

Attachments: BrightLane_testcases_manifest.csv (csv)

Looking forward — let me know your preferred runbook and the right folks on your side to loop in.

Best,
Samir Rao
Director, Data Science
BrightLane Retail

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: BrightLane evaluation exchange - sandbox + MAP proposal

Samir — thanks for the clear asks and the manifest. Summary below of what Redwood needs to proceed quickly:

Proposed MAP (high level):
- Week 0 (sign): sign narrow MPA (evaluation-only license) and transfer SLA
- Week 1 (ingest & smoke): BrightLane uploads artifacts to S3 staging; Redwood runs a guarded ingest into ephemeral sandbox; basic acceptance tests executed by both teams
- Week 2 (acceptance): acceptance tests run; feedback loop; close or extend by mutual agreement

Security & compliance checklist (minimum):
- Transfer: pre-signed S3 URL + one-time access key (we prefer short TTL; we will provide a temporary ingest IAM role)
- Data handling: repo-level KV cache disabled for the pilot; no retention beyond 30 days post-acceptance; documented destruction confirmation
- Audit: transfer and inference logs retained for 90 days and shared as CSV on request

Ben (CC) will own the ingest and acceptance criteria; Karthik will coordinate MPA/legal redline. If this aligns, we can send a DOCU-SIGN link for the MPA and an S3 staging target by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: Signed-MAP-draft.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir@brightlane.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLane evaluation exchange - sandbox + MAP proposal

Samir / team — quick technical checklist and acceptance knobs so we avoid rework:

1) Artifact format:
   - Prompt pack: single .zip, max 2GB, top-level README with mapping to manifest
   - Testcases: canonical CSV with id,input,expected and privacy flags for any PII
2) Ingest process:
   - We will share an S3 prefix (redwood-eval-staging/brightlane/DL-2027-BL-341/) and a short-lived STS role to upload
   - We will run an automated scan (no content preview) to surface PII flags; flagged records will be quarantined and handled via agreed exceptions
3) Sandbox runtime constraints:
   - Ephemeral instances; KV cache disabled; token-level debug logs collected but scrubbed for PII before sharing
   - Rate limits: capped at 5 RPS during acceptance testing to preserve QoS for other pilots
4) Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
   - >= 90% match on labeled testcases across the baseline model family (list attached)
   - No scoped PII leak incidents during the run

Operational asks from BrightLane:
- Confirm the final artifact names and a primary transfer point (who will upload).
- Sign the MPA (we will send the DocuSign link).

I have attached a short technical checklist and S3-transfer-instructions.pdf for your upload team. Grace, can you help ensure the ephemeral environment is ready by 2028-01-16?

Attachments: S3-transfer-instructions.pdf, BrightLane_eval_promptpack_v1.zip (zip)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
